ἀναστάσεως τὸ δεδεμένων τῶν χειρῶν καὶ τῶν ποδῶν καὶ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ἐξελθεῖν
περιπατοῦντα. διὰ τοῦ λύειν ἐμαρτύρουν, ὅτι οὐκ ἦν φάντασμα, ἀλλ' ὁ Λάζαρος ἦν.

διέβαλλον γὰρ ὡς τὸν τεθαμμένον ἀνασκάψαι ἐπιτάξαντα. εἶτά φησιν, ὅτι
συνήγαγον κατ' αὐτοῦ συνέδριον καὶ διελογίζοντο λέγοντες· ἐὰν ἀφῶ μεν αὐτὸν

ἐδίδουν αὐτὴν διαδεχόμενοι αὐτούς, ὅτε ἤθελον. 393 {3Jο 11, 49 51}3Στόματι
λαλοῦντι μόνον, οὐ μὴν τῆς τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος χάριτος ἁψαμένης αὐτοῦ τῆς

οὐδὲν δὲ ὠφελεῖ τινα τὸ προφητεύειν. ἁρμόζει κατὰ τῶν μὴ ὀρθῶς πιστευόντων
προλεγόντων δέ τινα, οἵτινες, ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ἐν «ἡμέρᾳ» κρίσεως τῷ κυρίῳ· «κύριε, οὐ

θεοῦ τοὺς πιστοὺς καλεῖ ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς τοὺς ἐξ ἐθνῶν τοὺς «μακρὰν» ὄντας καὶ

54}3Εἰς κατάκριμα τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀναχωρεῖ οὐ δειλιῶν καὶ ἡμᾶς διδάσκων ἐν ἀκμῇ

πάθους καιρὸν καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων φειδόμενος σωτηρίας.
english: A nearly identical sign of the resurrection was that he came out walking with his hands, feet, and eyes still bound. By untying him, they bore witness that it was not a phantom, but Lazarus himself.

From this it is clear that not all the Jews around Mary saw the resurrection of Lazarus, but some of them did, and those believed in Christ. The rest heard about it from the eyewitnesses and went down to the Pharisees, stirring them up against him as one who had dared something unholy. They accused him of ordering the buried man to be dug up. Then he says that they convened a council against him and debated, saying, "If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come against us on suspicion of tyranny and destroy our city." They said this out of envy, but it came to pass even though they did not expect it, when they crucified him.

They accused him of having dared to do something unholy, as one who had ordered the buried man to return. After so many proofs, they spoke as if he were a mere man, not knowing that he himself was the Christ, the worker of the signs.

"If," they say, "those who believe in him make him king, the Romans will come against us as men who had seized tyranny and strip us of everything." They said this because they would not endure the terrible consequences, so that he would be put to death. And when they killed him, the painful things came upon them.

When the priesthoods became purchasable, the priests no longer served for their whole lifetime or by lineage, but the Romans gave the office to whomever they wished, replacing them whenever they wanted.

It was given to him to foretell this for the honor of the priesthood, with a mouth that only spoke, while the grace of the Holy Spirit did not touch his heart—not as to a prophet. Prophesying without the Spirit benefits no one. This applies to those who do not believe rightly but foretell certain things. If on the day of judgment they say to the Lord, "Lord, did we not prophesy in your name?" they will hear, "I do not know you." So no one should be led astray by this. Prophecy is not the fruit of good works, by which we recognize the saints, but the whole work of the Spirit, even if it speaks through human instruments, that is, through human tongues.
Christ endured death for the common salvation of all.

The evangelist calls the faithful "children of God," those from the Gentiles—those who were "far off" and have become "near," joined into "one body" with Christ as their one head (John 11:52). Caiaphas foretells what he does not know, glorifying Christ by necessity, like Balaam.

He withdraws for the condemnation of the Jews, not out of cowardice, teaching us not to throw ourselves into dangers at the height of anger. He fled, waiting for the fitting time of his passion and sparing their salvation.

findings.checker_says: ἀνακάμψαι means 'to dig up' or 'to break up,' not 'to return.' The false accusation was that Jesus ordered Lazarus exhumed, not brought back.

findings.quote: Prophesying without the Spirit benefits no one.
findings.source_quote: οὐδὲν δὲ ὠφελεῖ τινα τὸ προφητεύειν
findings.checker_says: Source says 'prophesying benefits no one' generally, not specifically 'without the Spirit'. Adds a qualifier not in source.
findings.reviewer_note: 'without the Spirit' is added; Greek means prophesying in itself profits the prophet nothing. 'benefits no one' overstates.
